title: A smooth algebra is a retract of a standard smooth algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then there are an $R$-algebra $B$ which is standard smooth over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] (so $B\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ with $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j=1,\dots,c}$ invertible in $B$) and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $\iota:A\to B$ and $\rho:B\to A$ with $\rho\circ\iota=\mathrm{id}_A$, such that $B$, viewed as an $A$-algebra via $\iota$, is smooth over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth, line 590) and its proof (lines 601-683: Lemma 07CG lemma-syntomic-complete-intersection gives a relative global complete intersection C with retraction; B' = C[y_1..y_c], the map R[z_1..z_n] -> B'_g etale, Algebra lemma-etale-standard-smooth)

proof.text: (The relative global complete intersection $C$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-retract-relative-global-complete-intersection] (Stacks 07CG) applied to the smooth $R$-algebra $A$ there are $n,c\ge0$, $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $J=(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ and $C=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/J$ such that $C$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R$, the classes $\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c$ of the $f_j$ form a basis of the $C$-module $J/J^2$, and there are $R$-algebra maps $\sigma:A\to C$, $\pi:C\to A$ with $\pi\sigma=\mathrm{id}_A$ and $C$ smooth over $A$ via $\sigma$. As $R\to A$ and $\sigma$ are smooth, $R\to C$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](2).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), lines 601-605 ('Apply Lemma 07CG ... As C is smooth over R')

proof.text: (The split conormal sequence and the matrix $(c_{ij})$.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-localization-conormal-split] to $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $I=J$, $C=P/J$ and $a=1$ (so $C_a=C$, smooth over $R$ by step 1): the map $\mathrm d:J/J^2\to\bigoplus_{i=1}^nC\,\mathrm dx_i$, $\mathrm d(h\bmod J^2)=\sum_i\overline{\partial h/\partial x_i}\,\mathrm dx_i$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative], has a $C$-linear left inverse $t$, and $0\to J/J^2\to\bigoplus_iC\,\mathrm dx_i\to\Omega_{C/R}\to0$ is split exact, so $\Omega_{C/R}\oplus J/J^2\cong C^{\oplus n}$. Since $\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c$ is a basis of $J/J^2$ (step 1), $J/J^2\cong C^{\oplus c}$, and write $t(\mathrm dx_i)=\sum_{j=1}^cc_{ij}\bar f_j$ with $c_{ij}\in C$. Then for each $\ell$, $\bar f_\ell=t(\mathrm d\bar f_\ell)=\sum_i\overline{\partial f_\ell/\partial x_i}\,t(\mathrm dx_i)=\sum_j\bigl(\sum_i\overline{\partial f_\ell/\partial x_i}\,c_{ij}\bigr)\bar f_j$, and comparing coefficients in the basis gives $\sum_{i=1}^n\overline{\partial f_\ell/\partial x_i}\,c_{ij}=\delta_{\ell j}$ in $C$ (Kronecker delta). Moreover, tensoring $\Omega_{C/R}\oplus C^{\oplus c}\cong C^{\oplus n}$ with the residue field $\kappa(Q)$ of any prime $Q\subset C$ gives $\dim_{\kappa(Q)}\Omega_{C/R}\otimes_C\kappa(Q)=n-c$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), lines 606-617 (the short exact sequence 0 -> (+) C f_j -> (+) C dx_i -> Omega_{C/R} -> 0, split since Omega_{C/R} is projective; left inverse t, t(dx_i) = sum c_ij f_j, sum_i (df_j/dx_i) c_il = delta_jl)

proof.text: (The algebra $B'$, its retraction and the map $\theta$.) Let $B'=C[y_1,\dots,y_c]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; by the universal properties of polynomial rings and quotients $B'=R[x_1,\dots,x_n,y_1,\dots,y_c]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$. The inclusion $C\to B'$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth], so $R\to B'$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](2). The $C$-algebra map $\varepsilon:B'\to C$, $y_j\mapsto0$, is a retraction of $C\to B'$. Choose $\tilde c_{ij}\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ mapping to $c_{ij}$ and let $\theta:R[z_1,\dots,z_n]\to B'$ be the $R$-algebra map with $\theta(z_i)=\bar x_i-\sum_jc_{ij}y_j$; regard $B'$ as an $R[z_1,\dots,z_n]$-algebra via $\theta$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), lines 618-631 (B' = C[y_1..y_c] = R[x,y]/(f), retraction y_j -> 0, the map R[z_1..z_n] -> B', z_i -> x_i - sum_j c_ij y_j)

proof.text: ($\Omega_{B'/R[z]}=(y_1,\dots,y_c)\Omega_{B'/R[z]}$.) Write $\Omega'=\Omega_{B'/R[z_1,\dots,z_n]}$ with derivation $\mathrm d$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $I_y=(y_1,\dots,y_c)B'$. (a) Since $B'$ is generated as an $R$-algebra by the $\bar x_i,y_j$ and $\mathrm d$ is additive, satisfies the Leibniz rule and kills the image of $R$, $\Omega'$ is generated as a $B'$-module by $\mathrm d\bar x_1,\dots,\mathrm d\bar x_n,\mathrm dy_1,\dots,\mathrm dy_c$; in particular it is a finitely generated $B'$-module. (b) The map $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to\Omega'$, $h\mapsto\mathrm d\bar h$, is an $R$-derivation, so by the universal property and the basis $\mathrm dx_i$ of $\Omega_{R[x]/R}$ with $\mathrm dh=\sum_i\frac{\partial h}{\partial x_i}\mathrm dx_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis] we get $\mathrm d\bar h=\sum_i\overline{\partial h/\partial x_i}\,\mathrm d\bar x_i$. (c) As $\bar f_j=0$ in $B'$: $0=\mathrm d\bar f_j=\sum_i\overline{\partial f_j/\partial x_i}\,\mathrm d\bar x_i$. As $\theta(z_i)$ comes from $R[z]$: $0=\mathrm d\theta(z_i)=\mathrm d\bar x_i-\sum_\ell(c_{i\ell}\,\mathrm dy_\ell+y_\ell\,\mathrm dc_{i\ell})$, so $\mathrm d\bar x_i\equiv\sum_\ell c_{i\ell}\,\mathrm dy_\ell\bmod I_y\Omega'$. Substituting and using the identity of step 2 (which holds in $C$, hence in $B'$): $0\equiv\sum_\ell\bigl(\sum_i\overline{\partial f_j/\partial x_i}\,c_{i\ell}\bigr)\mathrm dy_\ell=\mathrm dy_j\bmod I_y\Omega'$. Hence every $\mathrm dy_j$ and then every $\mathrm d\bar x_i$ lies in $I_y\Omega'$, and by (a) $\Omega'=I_y\Omega'$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), lines 632-648 (in Omega_{B'/R[z]}: 0 = df_j - sum (df_j/dx_i) dz_i == dy_j mod (y)Omega; dz_i = dx_i mod sum B'dy_j + (y)Omega; hence Omega/(y)Omega = 0)

proof.text: (Localizing: $R[z]\to B'_g$ is of finite presentation with $\Omega=0$.) By step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-one-plus-ideal-annihilator] (Stacks 00DV, applied to the finitely generated $B'$-module $\Omega'$ and the ideal $I_y$) there is $g\in B'$ with $g-1\in I_y$ and $g\Omega'=0$. Put $B=B'_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], $\Omega_{B/R[z]}\cong(\Omega')_g=0$. Choose $\tilde g\in R[x,y]$ mapping to $g$; by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-polynomial-quotient], $B\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n,y_1,\dots,y_c,w]/(f_1,\dots,f_c,\tilde gw-1)$ as $R$-algebras, and therefore, as $R[z]$-algebras, $B\cong R[z_1,\dots,z_n][x,y,w]/(f_1,\dots,f_c,\tilde gw-1,\ z_1-x_1+\sum_j\tilde c_{1j}y_j,\dots,z_n-x_n+\sum_j\tilde c_{nj}y_j)$ (the last $n$ relations eliminate the $z_i$). So $B$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra and a finitely presented $R[z]$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], with $\Omega_{B/R[z]}=0$; that is, $R[z]\to B$ is unramified (even G-unramified) in the sense of Stacks, Algebra, Definition 00UT.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), lines 649-656 ('As Omega_{B'/R[z]} is a finite B'-module by Nakayama's lemma there exists a g in 1 + (y_1..y_c) that (Omega)_g = 0. This proves that R[z] -> B'_g is unramified, see Algebra Definition 00UT')

proof.text: (Smoothness of $B$, the maps $\iota,\rho$, and the rank of $\Omega_{B/R}$.) $R\to B$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization] (applied to the smooth $R\to B'$ of step 3), and $C\to B$ is smooth by the same node applied to the smooth $C\to B'$; hence $A\to C\to B$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](2). Put $\iota:A\xrightarrow{\sigma}C\to B'\to B$. Since $g-1\in I_y$ and $\varepsilon(I_y)=0$, $\varepsilon(g)=1$ is a unit, so $\varepsilon$ extends uniquely to a ring map $\varepsilon_g:B\to C$ with $\varepsilon_g(b/1)=\varepsilon(b)$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property], an $R$-algebra (indeed $C$-algebra) map; put $\rho=\pi\circ\varepsilon_g:B\to A$. Then $\rho\iota=\pi\varepsilon_g(C\to B)\sigma=\pi\sigma=\mathrm{id}_A$. Finally $\Omega_{B'/R}\cong(B'\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R})\oplus B'^{\oplus c}$ [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-polynomial-extension] and $\Omega_{B/R}\cong(\Omega_{B'/R})_g$ [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization]; with step 2 this gives $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak Q)}\Omega_{B/R}\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak Q)=(n-c)+c=n$ for every prime $\mathfrak Q\subset B$ (if $Q$ is the inverse image of $\mathfrak Q$ in $C$, then $(B\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R})\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak Q)=(\Omega_{C/R}\otimes_C\kappa(Q))\otimes_{\kappa(Q)}\kappa(\mathfrak Q)$).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), lines 657-659 and 672-674 (B'_g smooth over R; 'Set B = B'_g. Note that C -> B is smooth and has a retraction, so also A -> B is smooth and has a retraction'); the rank n of Omega is what Stacks calls 'smooth k-algebras of dimension n' (line 659)

proof.text: (The fibre over a prime of $R$.) Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, let $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $T=B\otimes_Rk$ and $P_k=R[z_1,\dots,z_n]\otimes_Rk\cong k[z_1,\dots,z_n]$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension]; $T\cong B\otimes_{R[z]}P_k$ is a $P_k$-algebra, finitely generated as a $k$-algebra (step 5). (i) $k\to T$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](1). (ii) $\Omega_{T/P_k}\cong T\otimes_B\Omega_{B/R[z]}=0$ and (iii) $\Omega_{T/k}\cong T\otimes_B\Omega_{B/R}$ [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change], so by step 6 $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak n)}\Omega_{T/k}\otimes_T\kappa(\mathfrak n)=n$ for every prime $\mathfrak n\subset T$. (iv) $k\to P_k$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth] and $\Omega_{P_k/k}$ is free with basis $\mathrm dz_1,\dots,\mathrm dz_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), lines 657-659 ('For any ring map R -> k where k is a field we obtain an unramified ring map k[z_1..z_n] -> (B'_g) (x)_R k between smooth k-algebras of dimension n'), taken for k the residue fields of R

proof.text: (Local rings at maximal ideals: regular of dimension $n$.) Let $\mathfrak m\subset T$ be a maximal ideal and $\mathfrak p'\subset P_k$ its inverse image. (a) $T/\mathfrak m$ is a field finitely generated as a $k$-algebra, hence finite over $k$ [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma]; $P_k/\mathfrak p'\subseteq T/\mathfrak m$ is a domain of finite $k$-dimension, hence a field (multiplication by a nonzero element is an injective $k$-linear endomorphism, hence surjective), so $\mathfrak p'$ is maximal. (b) $T_{\mathfrak m}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-fibre-regular-local] applied to the smooth $k\to T$ and the prime $(0)$ of $k$ ($T\otimes_kk=T$). $k\to T$ is smooth at $\mathfrak m$ ($g=1$ in [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]), so by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-dimension-differentials] and step 7(iii) the dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ at $\mathfrak m$ is $n$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-dimension-local-ring] $\dim T_{\mathfrak m}=n$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. (c) The same argument for $k\to P_k$ and the maximal ideal $\mathfrak p'$, using step 7(iv), shows that $(P_k)_{\mathfrak p'}$ is a regular local ring of dimension $n$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), line 661 (Algebra Lemma 00TS lemma-characterize-smooth-kbar: a finite type algebra smooth at a maximal ideal has regular local ring there, of dimension the rank of Omega). Stacks cites 00TS, which is stated for an algebraically closed field; for the residue field k used here the same facts come from Algebra Lemma 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609: the dimension at the point, and regularity) and Lemma 00OU (dimension at a closed point = dimension of the local ring)

proof.text: (The fibres of $P_k\to T$ are zero-dimensional.) With $\mathfrak m,\mathfrak p'$ as in step 8, let $F=T\otimes_{P_k}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$. It is a finitely generated $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$-algebra with $\Omega_{F/\kappa(\mathfrak p')}\cong F\otimes_T\Omega_{T/P_k}=0$ ([lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change], step 7(ii)), so by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-ring-map-iff-unramified-affine] $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is unramified and by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-algebra-over-field-product] $F\cong L_1\times\dots\times L_r$ with fields $L_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-localization-quotient], $F\cong T_{\mathfrak p'}/\mathfrak p'T_{\mathfrak p'}$, so $T_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak p'T_{\mathfrak m}$ is the localization of $F$ at the prime given by $\mathfrak m$; the localization of a finite product of fields at a prime is one of the factors, a field. Hence $\dim(T_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak p'T_{\mathfrak m})=0$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), line 658 ('unramified ring map k[z] -> (B'_g) (x)_R k'); the zero-dimensionality of the fibres of an unramified map is Algebra Lemma 00UW (lemma-unramified-at-prime), whose proof is the product decomposition used here

proof.text: ($T$ is flat over $P_k$, by miracle flatness.) For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset T$ and $\mathfrak p'$ as in step 8, $(P_k)_{\mathfrak p'}\to T_{\mathfrak m}$ is a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings; $(P_k)_{\mathfrak p'}$ is regular (step 8(c)); $T_{\mathfrak m}$ is regular of dimension $n$, so its maximal ideal is generated by $n$ elements, which form a regular sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], so $\operatorname{depth}T_{\mathfrak m}\ge n=\dim T_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]; and $\dim T_{\mathfrak m}=n=n+0=\dim(P_k)_{\mathfrak p'}+\dim(T_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak p'T_{\mathfrak m})$ (steps 8, 9). By [lem-weil-pbc-miracle-flatness] (Stacks 00R4), $(P_k)_{\mathfrak p'}\to T_{\mathfrak m}$ is flat. Now let $\mathfrak n\subset T$ be any prime, $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak n$ a maximal ideal, and $\mathfrak p''$ the inverse image of $\mathfrak n$ in $P_k$. $T_{\mathfrak n}$ is a localization of $T_{\mathfrak m}$, hence flat over it [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]; with the flat maps $P_k\to(P_k)_{\mathfrak p'}\to T_{\mathfrak m}$ we get $P_k\to T_{\mathfrak n}$ flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp], and since this map factors through the localization $(P_k)_{\mathfrak p''}$, $T_{\mathfrak n}$ is flat over $(P_k)_{\mathfrak p''}$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-map-local-criterion], $P_k\to T$ is flat (trivially so if $T=0$).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), lines 659-661 ('It follows that k[z_1..z_n] -> (B'_g) (x)_R k is flat by Algebra, Lemmas 00R4 and 00TS')

proof.text: ($R[z]\to B$ is flat, by the critère de platitude par fibres.) Let $\mathfrak Q\subset B$ be a prime, $\mathfrak p'\subset R[z]$ and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ its inverse images. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre] (Stacks 00R7) to $R_{\mathfrak p}\to R[z]_{\mathfrak p'}\to B_{\mathfrak Q}$ (local homomorphisms) and $M=B_{\mathfrak Q}$: (1) $R[z]_{\mathfrak p'}$ and $B_{\mathfrak Q}$ are localizations of the finitely presented $R$-algebras $R[z]$ and $B$ (step 5), hence also of $R_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RR[z]$ and $R_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RB$, finitely presented over $R_{\mathfrak p}$; (2), (3) $M$ is free of rank one over $B_{\mathfrak Q}$, nonzero; (4) by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-localization-quotient], $M/\mathfrak pM$ and $R[z]_{\mathfrak p'}/\mathfrak pR[z]_{\mathfrak p'}$ are the localizations of $T=B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $P_k$ at the primes given by $\mathfrak Q$ and $\mathfrak p'$, and the map between them is the localization of $P_k\to T$, which is flat by step 10 and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps]; (5) $B$ is flat over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat] (step 6), so $B_{\mathfrak Q}$ is flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps]. Hence $B_{\mathfrak Q}$ is flat over $R[z]_{\mathfrak p'}$ for every prime $\mathfrak Q$, and $R[z]\to B$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-map-local-criterion].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), lines 661-664 ('By the critère de platitude par fibre (Algebra, Lemma 00R7) we conclude that R[z_1..z_n] -> B'_g is flat')

proof.text: ($R[z]\to B$ is étale.) The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R[z]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] since $B$ is a finitely presented $R[z]$-algebra (step 5); it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] since its local rings are the maps $R[z]_{\mathfrak p'}\to B_{\mathfrak Q}$, flat by step 11 and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps]; and it is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism] by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-ring-map-iff-unramified-affine], since $B$ is a finitely generated $R[z]$-algebra with $\Omega_{B/R[z]}=0$ (step 5). So $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R[z]$ is étale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. (Stacks concludes with Algebra Lemma 00U6, lemma-characterize-etale, that $R[z]\to B$ is étale in the sense of Algebra Definition 00U1; with the definition of étale used in this DAG the three properties give it directly, and the agreement with 00U1 is [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine].)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), lines 665-667 ('Finally, Algebra, Lemma 00U6 implies that R[z_1..z_n] -> B'_g is etale')

proof.text: (An étale algebra has a square presentation with invertible Jacobian: the proof of Stacks 00U9.) Choose a presentation $R[z][w_1,\dots,w_m]\to B$ of the $R[z]$-algebra $B$ (step 5) with kernel $I$, a finitely generated ideal. By step 12 and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-conormal-criterion], $\mathrm d:I/I^2\to\bigoplus_{k=1}^mB\,\mathrm dw_k$ is bijective, so $I/I^2$ is a free $B$-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-conormal-free-presentation-basis] (Stacks 07CF, over the base ring $R[z]$) there are $s,t\ge0$, $g_1,\dots,g_t\in R[z][u_1,\dots,u_s]$ and an isomorphism of $R[z]$-algebras $R[z][u_1,\dots,u_s]/(g_1,\dots,g_t)\cong B$ such that, with $I'=(g_1,\dots,g_t)$, the classes $\bar g_j$ form a basis of $I'/I'^2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-conormal-criterion] again, $\mathrm d':I'/I'^2\to\bigoplus_{k=1}^sB\,\mathrm du_k$, $\bar g_j\mapsto\sum_k\overline{\partial g_j/\partial u_k}\,\mathrm du_k$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative], is bijective: the $t\times s$ matrix $(\overline{\partial g_j/\partial u_k})$ over $B$ is invertible. If $B\neq0$, reducing modulo a maximal ideal of $B$ gives a bijective linear map $\kappa^t\to\kappa^s$ of vector spaces, so $t=s$, and the square matrix has a two-sided inverse, so its determinant is a unit of $B$. If $B=0$, then $A=0$ (as $\rho\iota=\mathrm{id}_A$), and $B\cong R[z][u_1]/(1)$ with $s=t=1$ has unit determinant $0=1$ in $B$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CH (lemma-smooth-standard-smooth), lines 674-683 ('By Algebra, Lemma 00U9 we can write B = R[z_1..z_n, w_1..w_m]/(g_1..g_m) with det(dg_j/dw_i) invertible in B'), with the proof of Algebra Lemma 00U9 (lemma-etale-standard-smooth, lines 39272-39286: d is an isomorphism, Lemma 07CF lemma-huber gives a presentation with the f_i a basis of I/I^2, hence c = n and the determinant is invertible)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By step 13, $B\cong R[z][u_1,\dots,u_s]/(g_1,\dots,g_s)=R[u_1,\dots,u_s,z_1,\dots,z_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_s)$ as $R$-algebras, with the variables ordered $u_1,\dots,u_s,z_1,\dots,z_n$, and the determinant of $(\partial g_j/\partial u_k)_{1\le j,k\le s}$, the partial derivatives with respect to the first $s$ variables, is a unit of $B$: this is a standard smooth presentation [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] with $s+n\ge s$, so $B$ is standard smooth over $R$. Together with the $R$-algebra maps $\iota:A\to B$, $\rho:B\to A$ of step 6, $\rho\iota=\mathrm{id}_A$, and the smoothness of $A\to B$ via $\iota$ (step 6), this proves the lemma.

Proof in 14 steps following the proof of 07CH (smoothing.tex lines 601-683): 07CG (new node, its smooth case, with the basis property of J/J^2 from its proof) gives C = R[x]/(f) with retraction; the split conormal sequence (existing 07EZ-node smooth-localization-conormal-split, a = 1) gives the matrix (c_ij) with sum_i (df_l/dx_i) c_ij = delta; B' = C[y], theta(z_i) = x_i - sum c_ij y_j; Omega_{B'/R[z]} = (y)Omega written out; Nakayama (00DV node) gives g in 1 + (y), B = B'_g, finitely presented over R[z] with Omega = 0; smoothness of B over R and A, the retraction rho through the universal property of B'_g, rank n of Omega_{B/R}; fibrewise: residue field k, T = B (x) k, regular local rings of dimension n at maximal ideals (Zariski lemma, 00TT node, new 00OU node; Stacks cites 00TS, which is for algebraically closed fields), zero-dimensional fibres of the unramified k[z] -> T, miracle flatness (new 00R4 node), flatness at all primes; critère de platitude par fibres (new 00R7 node) gives R[z] -> B flat; etale by the DAG's definition (lfp, flat, unramified), replacing Stacks' appeal to 00U6; 00U9 written out (conormal criterion node, Huber 07CF new Mathlib leaf); standard smooth presentation by ordering the variables.
